When the facts are on your side it takes 5 seconds to google a good source that supports your position, on the other hand writing bullshit is tiring. I guess all I want to hear is what you guys use to deal with this kind of individuals. And I know, I know internet discussions derp...

Naturally, I'm talking in those cases when all the facts are on your side but whoever is arguing with you is trying to evade the insurmountable evidence with empty wordings, some classics would be "It's open to interpretations"/"It's subjective" (when it's not) or walls of text that once analyzed amount to nothing.

Extra points for those solutions that won't get you dirty (no personal attacks) and low effort but not retreating solutions! (However, I must admit that avoiding this sort of discussions is the wisest thing to do...)
When arguing, best ways to deal against rhetoric?

i just use logic, or simply state

"I disagree"

you be surprised how much this works.

When your opponent is pulling "it's subjective" card, they're essentially saying you didn't prove them wrong, only that you might be right. Did you prove them wrong? If you can, do so. Even if you can't, they've also implied that you're not wrong either.

Don't dismiss rhetoric as an empty, cheap tactic. It's the skill of convincing people; arguing is rhetoric. Bolster your conclusion with sources then logic, then point out any flaw in your opponent's source credibility or logic process. Be aware of what you and they are trying to prove respectively. When they "take advantage" of rhetoric, understand what exactly they're doing if you want to counter them. Sometimes they will say it's subjective; explain why it's not subjective. Sometimes they will push the burden of proof on you; ask what proof they want, and set the same standard against them. Sometimes they will try to destabilize your argument by luring you into answering questions you were not prepared for; ask yourself if it's relevant and respond accordingly.

Rule 1, your goal isn't really to convince them; it's to convince the people watching. Some people are not there to change their mind, only to assert theirs. Fine then, just continue as if you're trying to convince them. Present your argument and they will present theirs, and people who has an open mind will pick whichever they feel is the better.

Rule 0, debate isn't about winning, it's about learning. Once your goal becomes about winning, you'll end up with two people squabbling about who's right and who's wrong, and the only thing the audience can do is pick sides. Don't think your facts are "insurmountable". Once you're certain that you're irrefutably right, you have no motivation to think of contrary evidences, evidences that others might believe. It doesn't matter if something is true when other people believe it isn't. Also, people tend to distrust people who seems to be trying to win rather than argue.

Other than that, it's important to know how to avoid or back out from fruitless arguments. To which I offer these advises:

  1. Don't commit unless you're ready to go full in. If you back out without proper conclusion, people are going to assume you've given up.

  2. Don't let emotions decide if you should get involved into the argument. If your motivation is emotional, then your argument is in danger of being emotional.

  3. Always be aware of what you and they are trying to prove. The argument might pointlessly go in circles because you two are arguing two irrelevant points.

So I have listened to Hypnosis recordings before, and those definitely work for me. This is because hypnosis lets the listener go into a trance, allowing the message to become clear to the subconscious. However, other things such as binaural beats, subliminals, frequencies, visuals, and other shit don't really require anything from what I have observed. And so I see [bullshit like this in existence.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cwl8G35sjII) They explain that it happens at some subconscious level the consciousness can't detect.

So what is bullshit, and what isn't? Unfortunately there are only so many different hypnosis recordings on Youtube for my purposes.
Hypnotic content-What is bullshit and what isn't?

Have you ever said something, and then realized you heard it before? It's why brand impressions are the main goal of most advertising. It's why name recognition is so big in elections. And it's the most clearly recognizable example of suggestibility. If you see the Coca Cola symbol you're more likely to buy it. Even if you say advertising has no effect on you.

The part of hypnosis that's not bullshit is people letting themselves dream in suggested patterns and smoothly accept ideas that are a little further than they would otherwise accept. Besides the above example you cannot hypnotize someone into doing something they wouldn't otherwise do. You can use hypnosis to strongly remind someone at a later period. Or to reinforce things they already want to do. If you're suggestible and you smoke, and you want to quit, someone could hypnotize you into remembering that smoking isn't something you want to do. If you don't want to quit and you don't give a fig, that hypnosis would accomplish very little. It's possible that you could be made to forget the session, but if you didn't agree to be hypnotized it's very unlikely to have worked at all. And if you agreed to by hypnotized and then forgot the session, in the smoking example if you didn't care about smoking you would have an impulse not to, and wonder why, but smoke anyway.

Hypnosis is an extremely interesting and useful aspect of exploring the human mind. Unfortunately, as you point out, it's been overtaken by charlatans. Chances are if they're doing it on a stage it's about as real as any magic trick.

If you are asking for the scientific consensus on hypnosis compared to the scientific consensus on binaural beats, subliminals, etc. you can look it up in a scientific journal.

Hypnosis is basically an active relaxation feedback loop. A hypnotist watches your reaction while they say things in order to relax you. If you are becoming visibly more relaxed, then the hypnotist continues on, if not, then they stop and try something else. Tapes can work in some cases since there are reactions that are common in large swaths of the population. Tapes won't work for everyone though. On the other hand, a live hypnotists may not work all the time either.

Binaural beats, subliminals, etc. have not been found to have any scientific basis. It should be pretty easy (read cheap) to perform a study on any of these things. As far as I know, there haven't been any studies that show that binaural beats work.

The best way to determine if something that sounds pseudoscientific works is to ask yourself if someone is making money off of it without selling books. Subliminal messages work. Movie theaters use them to sell soda and popcorn. Binaural beats probably don't work because the only people claiming they do are the ones who are selling mp3s of binaural beats. If they did work people would use the frequencies that lower inhibitions in shopping malls, grocery stores etc.
